items.name: MiniMax M3.1 Flash
items.summary: MiniMax's 428B-parameter MoE text model (23B active) with 1M-token context and always-on reasoning across five effort levels, delivering ~3x faster inference and ~70% lower agentic-task costs than M3 at flat $0.15/$0.60 per million tokens; the anonymous "Space Bunny" checkpoint was an early build, and open weights are promised Oct 23.

items.name: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017
items.summary: An updated MIT-licensed checkpoint of DeepSeek's open-weight multimodal MoE Flash model, described as a Pareto improvement in performance and cost — gains on all 11 reported benchmarks — served under the existing deepseek-flash API name alongside new Search and Fetch APIs for agents.

items.name: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 (Super VL + Bolt)
items.summary: NVIDIA's three new open models purpose-built for always-on AI agents: Nemotron 3.5 Super VL, an open 120B-parameter (12B active) multimodal MoE model claiming frontier-class agentic accuracy at one-fifth the parameter count of NVIDIA's largest reasoning model, plus two Bolt edge models for data center to desktop.

items.name: Meta Muse Wonder & Muse Wonder Full
items.summary: Meta Superintelligence Labs' first frontier-class models, built around "Active Memory" (long-horizon user context) and "Active Focus" (persistent goal pursuit) for personal and professional agents; Wonder is on the Meta Model API at $4/$20 per million tokens while the stronger Wonder Full is Muse Code-subscription-only, and neither ships open weights — a notable shift from Llama.

items.name: Cloudflare Clairic
items.summary: Cloudflare's first "System One" extraction model, live in preview on Workers AI — instead of generating text it returns typed values (numbers, dates, lists, forecasts) from unstructured text and images in a single forward pass with zero output tokens at $0.10 per million input tokens, with open weights promised.
